wps.name: Simulation parity remainder
wps.brief:
Task: WP-4.7 (DEFERRED_REVIEW §3.6 'Small parity remainder' + PARITY_CHECKLIST P4): close the remaining simulation-side parity gaps with oracle fixtures where the harness reaches them.

(1) P4 dead player saved: World::save_level (crates/mc-sim/src/world/mod.rs, the save_level fn) must save a player that died and left loadedEntityList, as vanilla's World.playerEntities keeps it (World.java:934-945; Entity.setEntityDead vs World.setEntityDead; the level.dat Player compound with Health -17 / DeathTime 21 / empty inventory per PARITY_CHECKLIST P4), so the world reopens on the Game Over screen; the client shell already keeps Game::detached_player (crates/mc-client/src/game.rs) — use whatever the sim needs (a player snapshot held by World, as vanilla's playerEntities list) and make the reopen path create the dead player as vanilla does. Fixture: a tick scenario where the player falls to death (set_pos high + wait) then a save op, with the level.dat player dump (check the harness dump kinds in tests/golden/README.md; add a dump only if none covers level.dat's Player compound, additively in tools/oracle/java/harness and crates/mc-golden, documented).
(2) Stats autosave: StatFileWriter func_27178_d / func_27425_c / func_27420_b (the 100-tick countdown and the unsent-file write; StatsSyncher.java + StatFileWriter.java in the spec tree), run synchronously from the shell's tick (the client calls into stats on the schedule the Java has); relabel the wrongly 'deferred' tags DEFERRED_REVIEW §2.3 names; optional item (6) merging an existing stats_<user>.dat at start-up (func_27180_b) if it is pure local file logic. Fixture-neutral (stats are not in traces): unit tests in crates/mc-sim/tests/stats.rs.
(3) Removed references with a parity effect (DEFERRED_REVIEW §3.1 A, items 5): the projectile's shooter after it left loadedEntityList (entity/arrow.rs attack_entity_by_id: Peaceful bounce, difficulty scaling, knockback, alertWolves, the extra Math.random draw per EntityArrow.java:163 and EntityFireball.java:124) and the mob's look target (living.rs EntityView::of, EntityLiving.java:706-710 faceEntity before the isDead check): keep a snapshot (class, position, the fields the Java reads) of a removed entity held by the referrer, as the Java object would be. Also entity/dispatch.rs get_collision_border_size: return 1.0 for Fireball (EntityFireball.java:198-200) instead of recording a gap. Fixtures where the harness can set it up (an arrow in flight whose skeleton shooter is killed/despawned before the hit; a mob whose target item entity is removed), else unit tests with the reason.
(4) Container close timing (crates/mc-client/README.md 'Known deviations'; DEFERRED_REVIEW §3.6 item 2 and §3.2 b): run the craftingInventory.isUsableByPlayer close inside EntityPlayer.onUpdate's position (EntityPlayer.java:80-84) in tick N, so tick N+1's input goes to the game as in vanilla; this needs the player's open container to be visible to the sim's player update (a hook or the container held by the sim player): design the minimal change and make the client follow (crates/mc-client/src/gui/container/mod.rs where the screen closes; additive). The te_gone case of §3.1 A then shrinks to 'an explosion after the player's update'.
(5) Fix the stale docs WP-4.4 listed for 4.6's files (spawner.rs:24-32; living.rs:768-770; pig.rs:12-13 and :95-98; cake.rs:127; player.rs:824-827) — doc comments only.

Rust target: crates/mc-sim/src/{stats/**, entity/arrow.rs, entity/living.rs, entity/fireball.rs, entity/player.rs, entity/dispatch.rs (the one arm), inventory/container/**, world/mod.rs (save_level + the player snapshot)}, crates/mc-sim/tests/**, tests/golden/<area>/<new>/scenario.json (+ oracle expected.jsonl via regen; NEVER hand-edit), the golden registration files, tools/oracle/java/harness + crates/mc-golden only for an additive dump if (1) needs it, crates/mc-client/src/{game.rs (stats schedule + dead player reopen), gui/container/mod.rs} minimal and documented, docs/mappings.md, tests/golden/README.md rows, crates/mc-client/README.md (remove the fixed 'Known deviations' entries). All 226 default + 5 soak fixtures byte-identical (regen default and SOAK=only; check-reproducible.sh; check-sensitivity.sh). Simulation DoD + client DoD (build mc-app, cargo test --workspace, clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -Dwarnings, fmt, wasm check). Smoke: die by falling (set_pos 60 blocks up), wait for Game Over, quit; reopen the same --world: the Game Over screen is up and the dump shows the dead player; Respawn works. Report what remains open with the Java evidence.

wps.name: Client parity fixes from WP-4.1
wps.brief:
Task: WP-4.9: fix the client-side defects of docs/PARITY_CHECKLIST.md §2 and the rendering follow-ups of DEFERRED_REVIEW §3.6, verifying each against the vanilla client with the WP-4.1 recipe (PARITY_CHECKLIST §1.1/§11: the original jar on Prism's Java 8 with -Duser.home, nested Xwayland, xdotool; rebuild the helper launcher if build/screens/wp41 is gone — the doc has its source description; it is never committed).

P3: a dead player's view must still draw the hand, entities and tile entities: resolve the view entity through Game::render_view() (the world's entity, else Game::detached_player) in render/mod.rs (the early return and the with_entity_mut cache fills) and item_renderer/mod.rs (the hand), per RenderGlobal.java:253-266, EntityRenderer.java:501; the GuiInventory preview too if it has the same lookup. Verify with the 'death' station: on Game Over the dropped inventory items and the red-tinted arm are visible as in vanilla.
P5: F3 memory lines: fill DebugSources::{max,total,free}_memory from the process (e.g. /proc/self/statm or a small crate already in the tree; the Java shows the JVM heap, so document the stand-in), keep the vanilla text format.
P6: frame-rate cap: vanilla only sleeps for 'Power saver' (40 fps, EntityRenderer.java:369-411); Balanced/Max run uncapped. Map the performance option to Bevy's present mode (AutoNoVsync for Balanced/Max; the 40 fps sleep for Power saver via the existing frame pacing or a sleep as the Java does), keep WP-4.3's --vsync flag as an override, document in docs/RUNNING.md and the README; this is an owner-flagged decision (Gate 3 Q11, PERF.md): implement it as the vanilla default and note the override.
P7: portal.travel must start before the loading screen (EntityPlayerSP.java:58-59: playSoundFX before usePortal): flush that ClientSound to the SoundManager synchronously at the point the UsePortal request is handled, before the world change blocks the frame (crates/mc-client/src/game.rs + sound/).
P8: the first frame after loading draws untextured fluids/sky: the animated tiles must start with terrain.png's still images (RenderEngine: the atlas is the PNG until the first updateDynamicTextures writes a tile; check what textures/mod.rs initialises the FX tiles to and run one updateDynamicTextures before the first world frame if that is what vanilla's order gives — Minecraft.java startGame registers the FX and runTick updates them before the first render: cite). Verify with a per-frame screenshot script across a load.
P9 (to confirm): screenshot every frame of a world load and check the 'Building terrain' progress bar is drawn (LoadingScreenRenderer bar 100x2, green); fix if missing.
P10 (to confirm): compare terrain/mod.rs update_renderers' choice and order of renderers to rebuild, and the in-flight-jobs stop, against RenderGlobal.updateRenderers (RenderGlobal.java, the sorted-by-distance list, the per-frame count rule) and EntityRenderer.java:365-378/485-492 (the time budget renderEndNanoTime + 1/120 s at Balanced); make the policy match vanilla given equal frame rate, and re-measure chunks loaded after 6 s and 30 s on the g05 world (PARITY_CHECKLIST P10 table) with the dev and release binaries; report.
Segfault at exit when quitting within ~1 s of entering a world (PERF.md §7, 4 of 6 tries): a bevy_render compute-pipeline drop on a task-pool thread during driver unmap; fix the shutdown order (e.g. wait for pipeline compilation / drain the render world before exit, or exit via AppExit after one more frame) and prove it with 20 quick-quit runs.
Rendering follow-ups (DEFERRED_REVIEW §3.6 last row): the inventory preview's hurt overlay/shadow/fire via RenderPlayer's code path instead of its duplicate (gui/container/inventory.rs → render/player.rs), the pass-1 (translucent) section draw order nearest-first as WorldRenderer sorts (visible with fast graphics), anaglyph's second eye (EntityRenderer's two-pass loop with the colour masks: implement or document as accepted), and the f32 far-origin jitter: implement a floating origin (RenderList's posMinus 1024-block anchoring, RenderGlobal.java/RenderList.java) if it fits in this WP; otherwise write the design into docs/PERF.md §7 and report.

Rust target: crates/mc-client/** (render/, item_renderer/, debug.rs, game.rs for P7/P6/segfault, textures/ for P8, gui/loading.rs for P9, terrain/ for P10 and the pass-1 sort, camera.rs/terrain for the floating origin), crates/mc-app/src/main.rs (P6 option plumbing), docs/RUNNING.md, docs/PARITY_CHECKLIST.md (append a §13 'Wave F results' table: defect → fix commit → vanilla re-check evidence), README additively.
